name: EU AI Act Risk Classification
description: These questions place your AI system into one of the four risk levels of the EU AI Act: banned, high, limited, or minimal. Answer for the specific system and how you actually use it.

questions.prompt: Does the system rate or rank people by their social behaviour or personal traits, in a way that can lead to unfair treatment?
questions.helpText: A general 'social score' used to grant or deny access to services. Banned under Art. 5.

questions.prompt: Does it use hidden or manipulative techniques, or exploit vulnerabilities (age, disability, social situation), that could distort decisions and cause harm?
questions.helpText: Subliminal or deceptive techniques people are not aware of. Banned under Art. 5.

questions.prompt: Does it infer people's emotions in the workplace or in education?
questions.helpText: Emotion recognition at work or school is banned, except for medical or safety reasons.

questions.prompt: Does it categorise people by sensitive traits (such as race, political opinions, religion, or sexual orientation) using biometric data?
questions.helpText: Biometric categorisation that infers sensitive attributes is banned under Art. 5.

questions.prompt: Does it perform real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement?
questions.helpText: Banned under Art. 5, with narrow legal exceptions.

questions.prompt: Does it predict whether a person will commit a crime based only on profiling or personality traits?
questions.helpText: Predicting offences solely from profiling is banned under Art. 5.

questions.prompt: Does it build or expand facial-recognition databases by scraping images from the internet or CCTV?
questions.helpText: Untargeted scraping of facial images is banned under Art. 5.

questions.prompt: Can the system generate or manipulate images or video depicting child sexual abuse?
questions.helpText: Banned under Art. 5 as amended by the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). Providers must have technical safeguards in place by 2 December 2026.

questions.prompt: Can the system generate or manipulate sexual or intimate images of a real person without their consent?
questions.helpText: So-called 'nudifier' tools. Banned under Art. 5 as amended by the Digital Omnibus. Applies from 2 December 2026.

questions.prompt: Does it identify people from biometric data (for example facial recognition), other than the banned real-time use above?
questions.helpText: Remote biometric identification is high-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is the AI a safety component of a product, or a product itself, that must undergo a safety assessment?
questions.helpText: Answer Yes for AI in products covered by the EU product laws in Annex I, Section A, for example medical devices, in-vitro diagnostics, toys, lifts or radio equipment. AI in machinery, vehicles or aircraft (Annex I, Section B) gets its AI requirements through those products' own EU rules instead; since the 2026 amendment this includes machinery under the Machinery Regulation.

questions.prompt: Is it a safety component in managing critical infrastructure (energy, water, gas, or traffic)?
questions.helpText: High-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is it used in education or training to decide admissions, score exams, or monitor tests?
questions.helpText: High-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is it used to recruit, select, evaluate, promote, or monitor workers?
questions.helpText: Employment and worker management is high-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Does it decide access to essential services, such as credit scoring, insurance pricing, public benefits, or emergency dispatch?
questions.helpText: Access to essential private and public services is high-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is it used by or for law enforcement, for example risk assessments or evaluating evidence?
questions.helpText: High-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is it used in migration, asylum or border control, or in the administration of justice or elections?
questions.helpText: High-risk under Annex III.

questions.prompt: Is it used in any other sensitive area listed as high-risk in Annex III of the AI Act?
questions.helpText: A catch-all for the high-risk areas in Annex III not covered above.

questions.prompt: Does the system interact directly with people, for example a chatbot or virtual assistant?
questions.helpText: People must be told when they are dealing with an AI (Art. 50).

questions.prompt: Does it generate or change text, images, audio, or video, including deepfakes?
questions.helpText: Generative AI and synthetic media must be labelled (Art. 50).

rules.explanation: The system may fall under a banned practice of the AI Act (Art. 5), such as social scoring, manipulation, banned biometric uses, predictive policing, or — from 2 December 2026 — generating child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery. These uses are prohibited, so review urgently and get legal advice.

The system is used in a high-risk area listed in Annex III, or as a product safety component, so it is treated as high-risk. The full set of high-risk duties applies, including risk management, data governance, documentation, human oversight, and accuracy and security testing. These duties apply from 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III and from 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.
The system interacts with people or generates content, so limited-risk transparency rules apply (Art. 50). You must tell people they are dealing with AI and label AI-generated content.
